newsitem.title: GERMANY: British minister warns German on Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: British minister warns German on Eurofighter.

text.p: European credibility and cooperation would be damaged if Germany cannot find a way to finance its share of the four-nation Eurofighter combat jet project, British Defence Minister George Robertson told a German newspaper on Thursday.
"The concept of European defence makes little sense if we have to buy all our fighters from the United States," Robertson said in an interview with the Bild Zeitung.
"An exit by Germany would heavily damage the credibility of European cooperation."
Germany's finance and defence ministers were due to meet during the day to try to find a way to find the 23 billion marks ($13.3 billion) needed for 180 Eurofighters.
Britain has already placed orders for 232, while Italy and Spain have been waiting for a clear signal from Bonn.

Robertson said the Eurofighter prohject was important in strengthening Europe against American competitors in defence and space contracting. "Without the Eurofighter, we run the danger of losing the European aerospace industry," he said.
On Wednesday German Finance Minister Theo Waigel met Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, the German partner in the Eurofighter project.
They discussed the possibility of Dasa financing Eurofighter production with money it owes Bonn as repayment for loans it received for its Airbus commercial aircraft operations.
